### Subject: Opinion on buyback tax implications for an unlisted company post the Finance (No. 2) Act, 2024 amendment

## 2. Statement of Facts

Ashoka Distilleries Limited, an unlisted company, proposes to buy back 5,00,000 equity shares from its promoter shareholders at INR 450 per share (face value INR 10), effective after 1 October 2024, using the route permitted under Section 68 of the Companies Act, 2013.

## 3. Issue for Consideration

Whether company-level buyback tax under Section 115QA applies, and how the buyback proceeds are taxed in the hands of the recipient shareholders.

## 4. Relevant Legal Framework

- Section 115QA (as amended)
- Section 2(22)(f)
- Section 56(2)
- Section 10(34A)


## 5. Judicial Precedents Considered

- Not applicable / no specific provisions beyond the Income-tax Act general scheme.

## 6. Analysis

Pursuant to the amendments made by the Finance (No. 2) Act, 2024, effective for buybacks on or after 1 October 2024, the earlier company-level tax under Section 115QA has been replaced with a shareholder-level regime: the entire buyback consideration is treated as deemed dividend under Section 2(22)(f) and taxed as income from other sources in the hands of the shareholders under Section 56(2), subject to TDS under Section 194, while the original cost of acquisition of the shares becomes a capital loss to the shareholder.

## 7. Conclusion / Opinion

No buyback distribution tax is payable by Ashoka Distilleries under Section 115QA; the entire consideration received by the promoter shareholders is taxable as dividend income, subject to TDS under Section 194, with the original cost of acquisition available as a capital loss.

**Confidence level:** High (based on express statutory amendment)
